note:
LabelSets that name no Apple row. THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK.

`check-labelsets-are-derived.py` proves, offline and per locale, that a LabelSet's members are the values Apple pins at its row -- but only for the sets that DECLARE one. `check-new-labelsets-name-a-row.py` requires a declaration of every set added from now on, measured against the merge base. Between them sits this census: the sets that predate both rules. Nothing asked whether these work in every language, and the answer is UNMEASURED rather than no.

The list was 58 when it was written and is 61. The three added on 2026-09-20 -- `eventListColumnM`, `eventListColumnName`, `eventListColumnPosition` -- are not new LabelSets: they name no row and always did, and the guard's own parser could not see them because their declarations close on the same line as their last argument. The guard reads them through `check-labelsets-are-derived.py`'s parser now, and it refuses an addition only when the set named a row at the merge base.

Each entry carries what `Scripts/derive_label_variants.py` says about it, so the work is sized rather than guessed. `value` and `namespace` mean a row was found; `ambiguous` means several resolve and somebody has to pick the one that MEANS this control; `no-row` means an absence proof is what closes it.

DO NOT CLOSE THESE MECHANICALLY. Measured while writing this file: `trackTypeMaster`'s best candidate is `ChineseOnly_TI_BassAmpLabel_Master_lowercase`, a Bass Amp label whose value happens to match and whose meaning does not. A row that resolves is not the row a control is named by.
how_to_shrink: Give the LabelSet a `derivedFrom` naming its row, or prove there is none with an entry in docs/canon/LABELSETS-WITHOUT-A-ROW.json. Then delete its line here. Scripts/check-labelset-census-only-shrinks.py refuses any other direction.

eventListColumnM.measured_2026_09_20: 4 candidate rows in four different ten-locale signatures. Two are chord labels from ChordsKit (Maj / maj). The other two read `M` in English and split in Chinese: MAMixer's `M` reads 静音 -- mute -- in zh_CN, and Logic.framework's `M` reads `M`. A mute column plausibly takes the mixer's row, and plausibly is the whole trap: a reading of the Event List header on a Simplified Chinese Logic separates them, and nothing else does.

eventListColumnName.measured_2026_09_20: 18 candidate rows, and 17 of them carry ONE ten-locale signature: Name / 이름 / 名前 / Name / Nombre / Nom / Nome / Nome / 名称 / 名稱. The eighteenth is MAMixer's `name`, which differs from it only by case in en, es, fr and it. The key is ambiguous; the values are not. Closing it still needs somebody to say which row names the Event List's own column, and none of the eighteen is that answer by measurement.

eventListColumnPosition.measured_2026_09_20: 7 candidate rows in two ten-locale signatures, differing in exactly one locale: ja reads ポジション in four of them and 位置 in three. Every other locale agrees (Position / 위치 / Position / Posición / Position / Posizione / Posição / 位置 / 位置). Offline cannot decide it -- reading the column header on a Japanese Logic does, and guessing picks a Japanese word for a column nobody has looked at.

why_these_three_arrived_late: Added 2026-09-20. They are not new LabelSets: they named no row before this branch too, and `check-labelset-census-only-shrinks.py` could not see them because its own parser took the end of a declaration to be the next `\n    )` in the file. It reads the policy through `check-labelsets-are-derived.py`'s parser now. For contrast, the two Event List columns that DO name a row: `eventListColumnTrack` derives from logic-canon://strings/Contents%2FFrameworks%2FLogic.framework%2FVersions%2FA%2FResources%2FLocalizable.strings/en/Trk#value (`Trk`), and `eventListColumnLength` from the same table's `Length#und`. One row, all ten locales, nothing typed -- which is what these three cannot do yet.
